## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@5609ab52c568750a9d9597b7fb107e59ce94e5e2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 5609ab52c568750a9d9597b7fb107e59ce94e5e2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@5609ab52c568750a9d9597b7fb107e59ce94e5e2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 5609ab52c568750a9d9597b7fb107e59ce94e5e2
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

Capture will click "Start" (button text exactly "Start"). - #pause-screen with Resume, Map, Mute, Restart? - #map-screen overlay maybe drawn canvas; use DOM map panel with canvas? Draw map in canvas when state map. - #victory-screen. - #touch-controls with joystick and buttons (aria-labels). - #rotate-hint. - HUD in canvas. Accessibility: buttons. Let's write CSS carefully. Game code in js/main.js. Possibly ~2500 lines. Let's architect in pieces and write incrementally, testing. Data model: const TILE=16, COLS=30, ROWS=17, VW=480, VH=272. Rooms keyed: id -> {name, map:[x,y], theme, bg, tiles: array of strings, spawn points for enemies (type, tx,ty, patrol), items, shrine, exits [{side, to, targetX,targetY?}], boss?} Exits: define rects along edges: exit = { side:'right', y: 12..16? } We can auto-generate door opening in tilemap. When player reaches edge boundary within door y-range, transition. Simplify: tilemaps have open edges; transition triggered when player center beyond bounds or in door zone. Better explicit exit zone: {x: 29*16, y: 13*16, w:16,h:48, to:'B', entry:'left'} and entry points per room. On enter via left, place player at x=2*TILE, y=ground. Store room entry spawn points: {left:{x,y}, right:{x,y}, up:{x,y}, down:{x,y}}. Room transitions: fade out/in quickly, camera fixed per room. Boss room gates? skip. Tile collision: - solid '#' and 'B' (breakable?) - one-way '=' platform: only collide when falling and previous bottom <= platform top. - spikes '^' damage. - 'o' candle decoration (non-solid). - 'v' vine decoration. - shrine placed separately. Rendering tiles: Generate tile images once per theme using seeded noise. Each tile at 16x16, drawn onto 480x272 offscreen room layer at load. Then dynamic elements drawn. For background: draw gradient + architecture (arches, windows, columns) procedural per theme with parallax slight offset based on player x (rooms fixed, but subtle). Could cache room background too. Tile art: stone blocks with variation. Use helper pixel drawing functions and a seeded RNG. Need quality: draw bricks 16x8 with mortar dark, highlight top-left, cracks, moss. Platforms wood/stone. Spikes metal. Ceiling. Add background bricks darker. Background per theme: - 'crypt': dark purple stone wall, pointed arch window with moon/stained glass, columns, hanging chains. - 'ossuary': green-teal damp, water drips, bone piles. - 'tower': tall window with moonlight, rafters. - 'roof': night sky with moon, distant spires, rain. - 'chapel': rose window, pews, candles. Use functions. Lighting: overlay radial gradients around candles and player. Use offscreen 'light' canvas: fill rgba(4,2,10,0.55), then destination-out radial gradients at lights. Draw with globalCompositeOperation maybe simply draw lights additive glows and a vignette. Too much darkness hides art; use vignette only + additive glows. Particles: dust motes floating, blood on hit, ember pickups, dash afterimages, boss effects, rain in roof. Character sprite: Let me hand-design pixel art via arrays for idle. Use a 20x28 grid. Scale 1 => 20x28 at 480x272; that's reasonably large (10% height). Player collision 10x20 centered at feet. Let's design pixel character with palette: H = hair black (#14101c) / highlight (#2a2033) S = skin pale (#e8d7d5), shadow (#b99aa3) E = eye red (#ff4d6d) glow D = dress dark (#211326) d = dress mid (#3a1f3d) R = red accent (#a32547) W = white lace (#cfc3d9) B = boots (#0d0a12) M = metal sword (#cfd4e6) m = metal dark (#7a7f99) C = cape inner (#4a1633) Sprite frames 20 wide x 28 high. Let's draw idle 2 frames, run 6, jump, fall, attack 3, dash, hurt, dead. Hand-authoring many frames is heavy; we can use procedural limb drawing for movement and use pixel matrices for torso/head base. Perhaps compose from parts: - Draw head/hair/face at top (12x12) with hair bob. - Body dress as trapezoid with ragged hem, arms, legs. - Animation params control leg offsets, arm/sword angle, hair sway, skirt sway. Rendered at 2x? Internal 480 wide, 20px character is okay. Use ctx.fillRect with 1px. Procedural with integer positions can look pixel art. Better approach: create sprite sheet from matrices for a few poses, then transform (flip/rotate sword separately). I'll hand-write 4 poses (idle1, idle2, run1, run2, jump, attack) at 18x26. That's doable but error-prone. Procedural is more flexible. Let's do procedural character rendering function drawGirl(ctx, x, y, facing, state, t): - coordinate system: origin at feet center, y up negative. Use px units. - hair back layer, cape, legs, dress, torso, arms, head, hair front, sword. - Round shapes with fillRect rows: helper drawEllipsePixels(cx, cy, rx, ry, color) loops. At 480x272, character ~18x28. Pixel unit = 1. Use crisp. Character dimensions: height 26. head 8x8 at y -26..-18; torso y -18..-10; skirt y -12..-3; legs -4..0; boots. Colors: skin #ecd9d6, hair #120e18 with #2b2136 highlights, dress #1b0f22 with #40204a, trim #c9b8d8, accent crimson #b83255, eyes #ff5d7a. Animations: - idle: bob 1px, hair sway, skirt. - run: legs alternate forward/back, body lean, hair/cape trailing, arms swing. - jump: knees tucked, cape up. - fall: cape billow. - attack: sword arc drawn separately with additive glow; arm extended. - dash: leaning, afterimages. - hurt: flash. Sword: a rapier/longsword 18px, drawn from hand with rotation depending on attack progress (arc from -60deg to +40). During idle, sword sheathed on back maybe. Attack draws arc with trail. Enemies procedural: - Bat: 12x8 wings flap. - Crawler: skull spider 14x10, legs animate. - Wraith: 12x18 floating with tattered sheet, glowing eyes. - Knight: 14x20 armored with sword. - Boss: 40x48 pale abbess with halo, veil, long arms, rosary projectiles. Items: - Relic pickups: glowing icons (bat wings, veil/dash, heart). - Embers: small flame diamonds. - Shrine: stone altar with candle flame, active when touched. Boss fight: - Enter G, gate closes (solid tile? just invisible barrier), boss intro overlay text, health bar bottom. - Attack patterns: - Phase 1: floats, fires 3 rosary orbs in arc, teleports, summons 2 bats. - Phase 2 (<50%): ground slam shockwaves, radial orbs, faster. - Player attacks boss when close (boss low enough sometimes). Boss hovers around y=110; player can double jump to hit. Maybe boss descends periodically. Ensure beatable. - Boss HP 30; sword 1 dmg per hit with 18f cooldown => ~30 hits. Maybe 24. Phase change at 12. - On death: slow-mo, explosion, victory overlay with stats. Game loop: requestAnimationFrame fixed timestep accumulator 1/60. Render interpolated? keep simple 60fps fixed steps. On 120Hz screens, run multiple steps. Input: keydown/up; prevent scroll for arrows/space. Touch joystick: pointerdown on left zone, track; knob. Buttons with pointerdown/up, multi-touch. Use pointer events, setPointerCapture. Attack/jump/dash each set pressed flags consumed in update; jump buffer. Implement `input = {left,right,up,down,jump,jumpPressed,attack,attackPressed,dash,dashPressed}`. Keyboard sets; virtual sets. At each update, handle pressed then clear. Jump buffer: store jumpBufferT when jumpPressed; coyoteT. Physics values at 60fps: gravity 0.22 px/frame²; maxFall 4.6; jumpVel -4.0; moveSpeed 1.7; accel 0.35; friction 0.45; dashSpeed 4.4 for 10 frames; doubleJumpVel -3.6. At 480x272, tile 16, jump height = v²/(2g)=16px = 1 tile. Too low. Need jump ~3.5 tiles: v = sqrt(2*0.22*56)=4.96. Use jumpVel -5.0, gravity 0.24 => height 52px (3.25 tiles). Max fall 6. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable dark gothic pixel-art Metroidvania for phone/tablet, starring a gothic girl protagonist.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Game title: **Vesper’s Lament**.
- Use a browser-based, canvas-rendered 2D game with procedural pixel art and Web Audio; no external assets.
- Planned world has seven connected rooms, ability upgrades, combat, shrines, a map, and a boss.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game shell, title/menu/panel screens, HUD and mobile touch-control markup in `index.html`.
- Added responsive styling in `style.css`.
- Added procedural audio in `js/audio.js`.
- Added seven-room world definitions and tile collision helpers in `js/world.js`.
- Added procedural character, enemy, item, shrine, and boss art in `js/art.js`.
- Added tile layers and themed parallax backgrounds in `js/artbg.js`.
- `node --check` succeeded for `js/world.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/art.js`, and `js/artbg.js`.

### Active
- Implement the gameplay loop, rendering integration, controls, combat, room transitions, persistence, HUD, and UI wiring.
- Run the game in a browser, fix issues, and capture/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- No current blocker; repeated tool connection failures interrupted file creation, so the main game entry point has not yet been implemented.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current files and implement `js/main.js`, importing the existing world, art, background, and audio modules.
2. Add any necessary script/module wiring in `index.html`, then test gameplay and fix discovered issues.
3. Capture a small JPEG screenshot and inspect the latest image.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell, screens, HUD, and mobile controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout, panels, and touch controls.
- `js/world.js`: Room graph, tilemaps, exits, and room metadata.
- `js/art.js`: Procedural sprites and game entities.
- `js/artbg.js`: Tile layers and room backgrounds.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural sound effects and ambient music.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `index.html` currently loads `js/main.js`, which does not yet exist.
- The room data defines rooms A–G; the final world edit changed room C’s bottom spawn to `{ x: 22 * TILE, y: 12 * TILE }`.

- Deliver a playable game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

- Game title: **Vesper’s Lament**.
- Use a browser-based, canvas-rendered 2D game with procedural pixel art and Web Audio; no external assets.
- Planned world has seven connected rooms, ability upgrades, combat, shrines, a map, and a boss.

- Earlier syntax checks succeeded for `js/world.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/art.js`, and `js/artbg.js`.

### Active
- Implement gameplay loop, rendering integration, controls, combat, room transitions, persistence, HUD, and UI wiring.

### Blocked
- `index.html` loads `js/main.js`, but that file does not exist yet; gameplay cannot run until it is implemented.

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using the existing world, art, background, and audio modules.
2. Test gameplay in a browser and fix issues.
3. Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable dark gothic pixel-art Metroidvania for phones and tablets, starring a gothic girl protagonist.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest one.
- Use the existing procedural art, world, background, and audio modules.

## Decisions
- Game title: **Vesper’s Lament**.
- Use browser-based canvas rendering, procedural pixel art, and Web Audio; no external assets.
- The world has seven connected rooms, ability upgrades, combat, shrines, a map, and a boss.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, title/menu/panel screens, HUD, mobile touch-control markup, and responsive styling.
- Added procedural audio, seven-room world definitions and collision helpers, procedural character/enemy/item/shrine/boss art, and themed backgrounds.
- Earlier syntax checks succeeded for `js/world.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/art.js`, and `js/artbg.js`.

### Active
- Implement `js/main.js` for gameplay, rendering, controls, combat, room transitions, persistence, HUD, and UI wiring.

### Blocked
- `index.html` loads `js/main.js`, but the file does not exist; gameplay cannot run until it is implemented.

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using the existing world, art, background, and audio modules.
2. Run syntax checks and test gameplay in a browser; address defects.
3. Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI controls; loads the missing `js/main.js`.
- `js/world.js`: Room graph, tilemaps, exits, spawns, enemies, and room metadata.
- `js/art.js`: Procedural drawing functions, including `drawGirl`, `drawEnemy`, `drawItem`, `drawShrine`, and `drawBoss`.
- `js/artbg.js`: `buildTileLayer` and `drawBackground` room rendering.
- `js/audio.js`: `Sound` class, sound effects, and ambient music.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout, panels, HUD, and touch controls.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Canvas dimensions are 480×272; world tiles are 16px with 30 columns and 17 rows.
- Room data defines rooms A–G; room C’s bottom spawn is `{ x: 22 * TILE, y: 12 * TILE }`.
- Touch controls are present in HTML for movement, attack, jump, and dash; keyboard hints are A/D or arrows, Z, X, C, and M.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable dark gothic pixel-art Metroidvania for phones and tablets, starring a gothic girl protagonist.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Use the existing procedural art, world, background, and audio modules.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Title: **Vesper’s Lament**.
- Use browser canvas rendering, procedural pixel art, and Web Audio; no external assets.
- Include seven connected rooms, ability upgrades, combat, shrines, a map, and a boss.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, title/menu/panel screens, HUD buttons, mobile touch-control markup, and responsive styling.
- Added procedural audio, seven-room world definitions and collision helpers, procedural character/enemy/item/shrine/boss art, and themed backgrounds.
- Earlier syntax checks succeeded for `js/world.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/art.js`, and `js/artbg.js`.

### Active
- Implement `js/main.js` for gameplay, rendering, controls, combat, room transitions, persistence, HUD, and UI wiring.

### Blocked
- `index.html` loads `js/main.js`, but that file does not exist, so gameplay cannot run.

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using the existing world, art, background, and audio modules.
2. Run syntax checks and test gameplay in a browser; address defects.
3. Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and UI controls; loads the missing `js/main.js`.
- `js/world.js`: Room graph, tilemaps, exits, spawns, enemies, and room metadata.
- `js/art.js`: Procedural drawing functions, including `drawGirl`, `drawEnemy`, `drawItem`, `drawShrine`, and `drawBoss`.
- `js/artbg.js`: `buildTileLayer` and `drawBackground` room rendering.
- `js/audio.js`: `Sound` class, sound effects, and ambient music.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout, panels, HUD, and touch controls.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no gameplay implementation has been made yet.
- Canvas dimensions are 480×272; world tiles are 16px with 30 columns and 17 rows.
- Room data defines rooms A–G; room C’s bottom spawn is `{ x: 22 * TILE, y: 12 * TILE }`.
- Controls shown in the UI: A/D or arrows to move, Z jump, X attack, C dash, and M map.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable dark gothic pixel-art Metroidvania for phones and tablets, starring Pandora.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Use the existing procedural art, world, background, and audio modules.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest one.
- The protagonist’s name is **Pandora**.

## Decisions
- Game title: **Vesper’s Lament**.
- Use browser canvas rendering, procedural pixel art, and Web Audio; no external assets.
- Include seven connected rooms, ability upgrades, combat, shrines, a map, and a boss.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, title/menu/panel screens, HUD buttons, mobile touch-control markup, and responsive styling.
- Added procedural audio, seven-room world definitions and collision helpers, procedural character/enemy/item/shrine/boss art, and themed backgrounds.
- Earlier syntax checks succeeded for `js/world.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/art.js`, and `js/artbg.js`.

### Active
- Implement `js/main.js` for gameplay, rendering, controls, combat, room transitions, persistence, HUD, and UI wiring.
- Test gameplay in a browser, fix defects, and capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.
- Use Pandora’s name consistently in the game’s text and presentation.

### Blocked
- `index.html` loads `js/main.js`, but that file does not exist, so gameplay cannot run.

## Next Move
1. Implement `js/main.js` using the existing modules and DOM controls.
2. Ensure player-facing references identify the protagonist as Pandora.
3. Run syntax checks and test gameplay in a browser; address defects.
4. Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

- `index.html`: Game shell and UI controls; loads the missing `js/main.js`.

- `js/artbg.js`: `buildTileLayer` and `drawBackground` room rendering.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
